calendar_reconciliation.interpretation: Of 5 zero-demand week(s), 5 overlap a configured closure period, 0 do not overlap a configured closure, and 0 cannot be assessed because calendar coverage is absent. Overlap is descriptive and does not establish that closure alone caused zero demand.

trend_interpretation.summary: The fitted linear trend is positive at 5.45 units per week, equivalent to 0.0705% of mean weekly demand per week. The last 13-week average is 28.1% higher than the first 13-week average. This compares two windows and does not by itself establish a sustained increase.

quarterly_seasonality_interpretation.summary: Q3 has the highest average weekly demand and Q2 the lowest among the observed calendar quarters. Q3's average is 54.5% above Q2's average in this observed dataset. This is an observed quarter-level difference, not confirmation of stable seasonality.

annual_profile_interpretation.summary: Valid year-pair correlations range from -0.279 to 0.627. Interpret them alongside the number of overlapping weeks; partial years are not directly comparable to full years. Correlation alone does not confirm repeatable seasonality.

2023_vs_2024.interpretation: The paired annual weekly profiles have a negative correlation (r=-0.279) across 13 overlapping ISO weeks. This is descriptive similarity, not proof of stable or causal seasonality.

2023_vs_2025.interpretation: The paired annual weekly profiles have a positive correlation (r=0.267) across 13 overlapping ISO weeks. This is descriptive similarity, not proof of stable or causal seasonality.

2023_vs_2026.interpretation: Not interpreted as a reliable correlation because the pair has fewer than 10 overlapping ISO weeks or insufficient variation in one or both profiles.

caveats: All observations and calendar closure periods are synthetic; they represent generator assumptions, not verified real-world market behavior or official holiday declarations.
Quarterly averages and annual profile correlations are descriptive diagnostics; neither proves that seasonality is stable or will persist in the forecast horizon.
Calendar closure overlap helps explain recorded zero-demand weeks but does not prove closure alone caused zero demand or capture latent/unfulfilled customer demand.
The analysis uses Monday-Sunday weekly bins and assigns each bin to a quarter using week_start; first or last bins may be partial relative to the configured data window.

The fitted linear slope summarizes an overall linear direction and does not mean demand changes by the same amount every week. The first-versus-last 13-week comparison is not a substitute for time-based model evaluation.

Calendar reconciliation found 5 zero-demand week(s) overlapping configured closure periods, 0 without a configured closure, and 0 not assessable due to missing calendar coverage. Review these distinctions before interpreting zero demand.
The calendar covers 2023-10-01 through 2026-09-30; 1 demand week(s) have partial daily-calendar coverage. Do not interpret missing dates in a partial week as non-business days or closure days.
